around.headline: BMTC head constable assaulted after alleged misconduct with a woman on a bus
around.summary: A head constable was assaulted after alleged misconduct with a woman passenger on a BMTC bus in Bengaluru. If you witness harassment on public transport, alert the driver/conductor immediately and note the bus number — BMTC and police can act faster with specifics.

around.headline: Bengaluru man says he got 'irritated' after woman asked, 'haven't you seen a girl wearing shorts?'
around.summary: A public altercation broke out after a man reportedly commented on a woman's clothing and she called him out; he later cited being 'irritated' as his reason. It's a reminder that calling out this kind of comment in a crowded, public place is generally safer than a private confrontation.

around.headline: KSR Bengaluru–Kozhikode Express to skip KSR Bengaluru station
around.summary: The KSR Bengaluru–Kozhikode Express will no longer halt at KSR Bengaluru station. Check your PNR and revised boarding point on the IRCTC app before your next trip on this route.

around.headline: Namma Metro's Pink Line to get two-wheeler parking at 4 stations
around.summary: Two-wheeler parking is being added at four Pink Line stations, with rates and an opening timeline expected soon. Useful if you've been driving the full way because of nowhere to park near a metro station.

around.headline: Cauvery water row: panel directs Karnataka to release 4 tmcft to Tamil Nadu over 15 days, sparking protests
around.summary: A tribunal panel has ordered Karnataka to release 4 tmcft of Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu over the next 15 days, triggering protests in the state. Watch local news for possible protest-related road closures in the coming days, separate from the already-scheduled July 31 supply maintenance cut.

around.headline: Bengaluru restaurants set August 15 deadline to quit Swiggy and Zomato over commissions
around.summary: Restaurant associations say they'll boycott Swiggy and Zomato from August 15 unless the platforms cut commissions and discount pressure. If that holds, expect some of your regular restaurants to disappear from delivery apps or push you toward direct ordering/other apps like Rapido's Ownly.

around.headline: US Senate advances Russia sanctions bill proposing 100% tariffs on India and China
around.summary: A bill advancing in the US Senate proposes tariffs of up to 100% on India and China over their Russia ties. If it moves forward, it's a real risk to India's export-heavy sectors and could ripple into IT/manufacturing jobs and stock market volatility here.

street_smart.title: You're at a friend's private party in a Bengaluru villa when police suddenly show up for a raid — turns out neighbours complained and it's being treated as a rave. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Real incident today: police raided a private villa party in HSR Layout, Bengaluru and arrested three people over a rave-party complaint. The source doesn't detail what happened during the raid itself, so this scenario is built around standard, well-documented guidance on how to conduct yourself if police raid a gathering you're at — it isn't a claim about what these specific three people did (The Hindu).
street_smart.situation: The music's still playing when the door bursts open — uniforms, torches, and everyone in the room suddenly unsure what happens next.

choices.text: Stay put, stay calm, and cooperate — show ID when asked, don't argue, and don't touch or hide anything, yours or anyone else's.
choices.feedback: Correct. Running, hiding, or handling other people's belongings during a raid can turn an innocent bystander into a suspect. Calm cooperation with your hands visible is the single biggest thing that keeps you out of trouble you didn't cause.

choices.text: Quickly delete photos, messages, or anything on your phone that might look bad before an officer gets to you.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Deleting content once police are present can be treated as tampering with evidence — a separate offence on top of whatever was actually happening at the party, and it can make an innocent person look guilty. An untouched phone is your best defence, not your biggest risk.

choices.text: Try to slip out through a back door or window before officers reach you.
choices.feedback: Fleeing a location being raided reads as evasion, even if you've done nothing wrong, and can turn a bystander into someone police now specifically want to question. If you're not doing anything illegal, staying is safer than running.

choices.text: Refuse to answer any questions or give your name until a lawyer arrives.
choices.feedback: You do have the right to a lawyer for formal questioning, but flatly refusing basic ID or cooperation on the spot tends to escalate things and can get you held longer than necessary. Give basic identification, stay polite, and save 'I want my lawyer' for if you're actually being formally questioned or detained at a station.

takeaways: If a gathering you're at gets raided and you've done nothing illegal, calm cooperation beats silence or flight — give ID, don't obstruct, don't touch other people's belongings.
Deleting photos, chats, or files once police are present can itself be a crime (evidence tampering) — often worse than whatever was on your phone to begin with.

You have the right to call a lawyer or family member before giving any formal statement or agreeing to a device search — ask for this clearly and calmly if detained, rather than refusing all cooperation at the door.

quiz.q: In India, deliberately destroying or hiding evidence during a police investigation is treated as:
options: Not an offence if it's your own evidence
An offence only for the main suspect
quiz.why: This applies to anyone present, not just the person under suspicion — which is why deleting things during a raid can create a new legal problem out of nothing.

quiz.q: The Cauvery water-sharing dispute in the news today is between Karnataka and which other state?
quiz.why: The river originates in Karnataka's Kodagu district and flows into Tamil Nadu, making it a decades-old interstate water-sharing flashpoint.
